**Reproduced on 1.15.13 — swallowed title-gen failure hid an actionable HTTP 400**

Concrete instance of swallowed title-generation failure (`ensureTitle` wrapped in `Effect.ignore` in `session/prompt.ts`). Version: opencode 1.15.13.

Symptom: new sessions stayed titled "New session". I didn't see any warning at the default log level; I only found the cause with `--log-level DEBUG`.

What the debug log showed:
1. The configured `small_model` (`openai/gpt-5-mini`) returned `model_not_found` (unavailable for my account).
2. The title call then routed to the session model instead of a small model — log fields `small=false agent=gandalf`, `providerID=github-copilot modelID=claude-opus-4.7`.
3. That call sent `reasoning_effort: "low"`, which the model rejected:
   ```
   HTTP 400 invalid_reasoning_effort:
   reasoning_effort "low" is not supported by model claude-opus-4.7; supported values: [medium]
   ```
4. The 400 was swallowed by `Effect.ignore`, so the session silently kept its default title.

Repro I used:
1. In `opencode.jsonc`: session model `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.7`, `small_model` set to `openai/gpt-5-mini` (unavailable for my account — any model returning `model_not_found` for yours should do).
2. Start a new session and send a first prompt (title generation fires on the first message).
3. Title stays "New session"; the 400 appears only at DEBUG level.

Workaround: set `small_model` to a model available for my account (`openai/gpt-5.4-mini`); the title call then routes `providerID=openai modelID=gpt-5.4-mini small=true agent=title` and succeeds.

The underlying error was actionable (unavailable small model + an incompatible param on the session-model call), but the silent swallow meant it couldn't be diagnosed without reading the DEBUG log. A single `WARN` like "title generation failed: <error>" would surface the cause without DEBUG-level log inspection. Related: #29737 (logging) and #27939 (configurable fallback chains via `agent.title.fallbacks`). See also #20269 for the effort-parameter angle.

**1.15.13: `reasoning_effort: "low"` reached a title-generation call and 400'd (GitHub Copilot)**

On 1.15.13, when my configured `small_model` (`openai/gpt-5-mini`) returned `model_not_found`, the title call routed to the session model (`small=false agent=gandalf`, `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.7`) and carried `reasoning_effort: "low"`. The API rejected it:
```
HTTP 400 invalid_reasoning_effort:
reasoning_effort "low" is not supported by model claude-opus-4.7; supported values: [medium]
```
The response reported supported values `[medium]`, so `low` fails on that path. The error is swallowed (`Effect.ignore` in `session/prompt.ts`), so the session silently stays "New session" (more on the swallow in #29734).

Workaround: set `small_model` to a model available for my account (`openai/gpt-5.4-mini`), which avoids the session-model path entirely.

What I could **not** confirm: whether the same effort value also reaches the *normal* small-model path, or only this case where the title call routed to the session model. In mine it was specifically the session-model call (`small=false`).

Repro: `opencode.jsonc` with session model `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.7` and `small_model` set to a model unavailable for your account; start a session and send a prompt; the new session stays "New session" and DEBUG logs show the `invalid_reasoning_effort` 400. Version 1.15.13.

I found the root cause. This is a confirmed upstream interaction between OpenTUI and foot terminal, tracked in:
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/24077 and #27496 (opencode)
- https://codeberg.org/dnkl/foot/issues/2335 (foot)

**What's actually happening**
On startup, OpenTUI (the renderer opencode uses) sends terminal capability queries. One of them is the kitty OSC 99 notification query:
\x1b]99;i=opentui-notifications:p=?;\x1b\
This is used to detect whether the terminal supports the kitty desktop‑notification protocol so opencode can show a native attention notification.

Foot receives the query and tries to format a reply. The reply is 166 bytes of metadata (lists of p=, a=, o=, u=, s=… fields describing what notifications it can do). Foot's reply buffer in osc.c::kitty_notification is only 128 bytes:
```
// foot osc.c (around line 765), pre‑1.27.0
char reply[128];  // ← too small
xsnprintf(reply, sizeof(reply), "\x1b]99;i=%s:p=?;p=%s:a=%s:…", …);
xvsnprintf returns "No buffer space available", which foot treats as a fatal error:
err: xsnprintf.c:42: xvsnprintf: No buffer space available
Thread 1 "foot" received signal SIGABRT, Aborted.
   #0  pthread_kill
   #1  raise
   #2  abort
   #3  fatal_error
   #4  xvsnprintf
   #5  xsnprintf
   #6  kitty_notification      ← OSC 99 handler
   #7  osc_dispatch
   …
```

SIGABRT tears down the whole foot process, so the window disappears, not just opencode. This also explains why it reproduces in xterm/Terminator/GNOME Terminal in #24077: any terminal that doesn't implement OSC 99 properly when receiving the query (or that runs an old/afflicted foot version) can crash. The same printf '\e]99;i=123:p=?;\e\\' from a shell reproduces it on a vulnerable foot.

**Why it works in kitty/alacritty/gnome-terminal**
- kitty/alacritty: ignore unknown OSC 99 queries (or don't claim the kitty notification id), so no reply is formatted, no crash.
- gnome-terminal (VTE): same, silently ignored.
- foot: actually implements OSC 99 and tries to answer — and answers too verbosely for its own buffer.

**Why OpenTUI 0.3.1 doesn't fully protect you**
The maintainers added a foot‑specific code path in zig/terminal.zig:
self.is_foot = self.term_info.from_xtversion and
  std.ascii.indexOfIgnoreCase(self.getTerminalName(), "foot") != null;
// …and a TERM env fallback:

  std.ascii.indexOfIgnoreCase(term, "foot") != null;

But is_foot is only true at query time if either:
1. term_info.from_xtversion is already true (the response would have been received earlier in a prior renderer instance — not the case at first start), or
2. TERM env var contains the substring foot.
If your TERM is xterm-256color, alacritty, tmux-256color, etc., the foot guard never engages and the OSC 99 query goes out anyway. Many distros (Arch/Artix, Debian sway, Gentoo) ship xterm-256color as the default for foot in some setups, which is exactly the configuration the affected users have.

**Fixes (any one of these resolves it)**
1. Upgrade foot to ≥ 1.27.0 — the foot maintainer (dnkl) shipped the buffer‑size fix in commit "osc: kitty notifications: increase query reply buffer size" on 2026‑05‑14.
2. Downgrade opencode to ≤ 1.14.48 — confirmed working by multiple reporters.
3. Set TERM=foot (or foot-extra) in the environment where you launch opencode. This flips OpenTUI's is_foot to true and the OSC 99 query is suppressed.
